before.name: Organelles and cellular compartments
before.tldr: A cell has compartments with different jobs. A molecule inside one compartment may still be separated from the place where it needs to act.
before.summary: The nucleus houses most cellular DNA; mitochondria have their own genome and participate in energy metabolism and other processes. Ribosomes make polypeptide chains. The endoplasmic reticulum and Golgi process and sort selected membrane or secreted cargo, while lysosomes degrade delivered material in an acidic compartment. That itinerary is not the route of every protein. Cytosol is the fluid outside membrane-bound organelle interiors; cytoplasm includes cytosol and structures outside the nucleus. A vesicle lumen is not cytosol.

links.label: NHGRI: DNA in nuclei and mitochondria
Induction of apoptotic program in cell-free extracts: requirement for dATP and cytochrome c.

notes: Endoplasmic reticulum and estrogen receptor are different meanings of ER; use the full name when context is unclear.
Localization, colocalization, amount, interaction and function need different evidence. More or brighter organelle staining does not by itself measure the rate of material passing through a pathway.

Mitochondria have roles beyond ATP production. Liu and colleagues used cell-free extracts and cytochrome-c depletion/add-back experiments to examine an apoptotic mechanism; this is a defined experimental result, not a universal measurement of cell death.

Among cytosolic ribosomes, some are free and others sit on the cytosolic face of rough ER, outside its lumen. Consider one secreted protein: it enters the ER lumen during synthesis, travels through the lumens of transport vesicles and Golgi compartments, and can leave when a secretory vesicle fuses with the cell membrane. Movement within these membrane-enclosed spaces is not cytosolic escape. This selected route does not describe every protein; a compartment diagram alone does not measure transport, activity or treatment effect.

A nucleus has an inner and an outer membrane, pores and DNA associated with proteins as chromatin. Rough endoplasmic reticulum forms a membrane network with a lumen; its membrane connects with the outer nuclear membrane. The Golgi consists of flattened membrane sacs, while a lysosome encloses material for breakdown. A mitochondrion has outer and inner membranes; folds of the inner membrane are cristae, and the matrix lies inside it. Its genome is distinct from nuclear chromatin. This general description is not an inventory of every human cell subtype, nor proof that DNA can never occur elsewhere.

before.name: Cell membrane
before.tldr: The cell membrane forms a selective boundary. Binding at the surface, entering a vesicle and reaching the cell’s internal working fluid are different steps.
before.summary: A lipid bilayer and its proteins separate the cell from its surroundings. Permeability depends on size, charge and chemical properties, rather than a universal small-molecule versus antibody rule. Passive movement follows the relevant gradient; active transport uses energy directly or through a coupled gradient. Endocytosis encloses material in a membrane-bound compartment. Delivery to cytosol or another target compartment requires further steps. Cytosol is fluid outside organelle interiors; cytoplasm includes that fluid and structures outside the nucleus.
notes: Surface-associated fluorescence does not establish internalization or cytosolic delivery. A membrane-exclusion dye tests the integrity property resolved by that assay; it does not certify every cell function.

In an inward-budding uptake example, an open pocket remains continuous with extracellular fluid until it pinches off. Once sealed, the vesicle is inside the cell but its contents are still in a membrane-enclosed lumen rather than free in cytosol. A process arrow does not make the cargo cross the bilayer. A receptor can span the membrane and bind a ligand outside; binding alone does not establish internalisation, cytosolic delivery or signalling.

In a phospholipid bilayer, heads face the watery surroundings on either side and tails face a shared inner core. An open ion channel provides a selective pore through that boundary. Net movement of a permitted ion follows its electrochemical gradient, which combines concentration and electrical effects; a drawing of inward flow does not set the direction for every ion or cell. This example is passive transport, rather than an ATP-driven pump or a route for a large cargo molecule. Uptake into a vesicle and escape across its membrane are separate events.

before.name: Mutation
before.tldr: A DNA variant describes a sequence change relative to a reference. Its origin, effect and clinical importance require separate evidence.
before.summary: A single-nucleotide substitution changes one base. Insertions and deletions change sequence length; copy-number and structural alterations affect larger regions and can overlap in category. In a specified coding transcript, missense changes alter an amino acid, synonymous changes preserve it, and nonsense changes introduce a stop. A net coding indel not divisible by three can shift the reading frame; an indel outside coding sequence is not automatically a frameshift. Transcript and reference versions determine the description.

links.label: HGVS: measured and predicted sequence consequences
NHGRI: three-base reading frames and frameshift variants
HGVS: protein deletions and predicted consequences
HGVS: deletion-insertion consequences, including inserted stop codons

notes: A DNA rearrangement, a joined RNA and a protein fusion are different observations. A predicted splice or protein consequence remains a prediction until supported at the relevant molecular level. Synonymous does not mean incapable of affecting RNA processing. Preserve genome build, accession/version, tested regions, detectable change classes and limits; pathogenicity or drug sensitivity does not follow from variant class alone.

In a specified coding transcript, an insertion or deletion of a complete number of three-base groups can preserve the downstream reading frame. It can still add or remove amino acids, change a codon at the join or introduce a stop; preserving the frame does not establish preserved protein function. The actual sequence and transcript consequences need checking. A protein-level change inferred from DNA remains a prediction until supported at the relevant molecular level.

Consider an invented internal coding-DNA window, read from the 5-prime to the 3-prime end with the same left-hand frame: ATG GAA TCC GCT AAC GGT, 18 bases. Changing A to C at reference position 5 gives ATG GCA TCC GCT AAC GGT and preserves the grouping. Deleting positions 4 to 6, GAA, gives ATG TCC GCT AAC GGT, 15 bases. Deleting only G at position 4 instead gives ATG AAT CCG CTA ACG GT, 17 bases, with changed downstream grouping. The final GT is an incomplete part of a continuing window, not a stop codon. These predictions assume the specified coding transcript and unchanged splicing; neither RNA processing nor translation was measured.

In another invented example, two DNA arrangements U-V-W and X-Y-Z become U-V-Z and X-Y-W. Each segment occurs once across the pair before and after this exchange. That stipulated copy-preserving example does not make every rearrangement copy-neutral. The new DNA adjacency alone does not demonstrate a joined RNA, a protein fusion, altered function, dependence on that function or treatment benefit.

before.name: Nonsense-mediated RNA decay
before.tldr: A cell can reduce some RNA messages when translation stops in an unexpected context. A predicted early stop does not guarantee that every message or protein disappears.
before.summary: Nonsense-mediated decay is RNA surveillance coupled to translation termination. Splicing can leave exon junction protein complexes near later joins in the message. Translation can remove junction-associated proteins; early termination while an appropriate complex remains downstream can help recruit decay machinery in one human route. Stop position, exon architecture, proximity to the start and other transcript features affect susceptibility. A common junction-distance shortcut is a hypothesis, not a universal clinical cutoff.

links.label: The exon-exon junction complex provides a binding platform for factors involved in mRNA export and nonsense-mediated mRNA decay.
Translation is required to remove Y14 from mRNAs in the cytoplasm.
Intron function in the nonsense-mediated decay of beta-globin mRNA: indications that pre-mRNA splicing in the nucleus can influence mRNA translation in the cytoplasm.
The rules and impact of nonsense-mediated mRNA decay in human cancers.
Litchfield et al.: frameshift expression, decay escape and immune evidence (2020)

notes: Human-cancer analyses found that a model containing several rules described RNA effects better than the junction rule alone; compensation could mask loss at gene level. Test the relevant transcript or allele with controls for RNA quality and cell mixture. Protein identity, persistence and function need separate measurements: RNA decay is distinct from protein degradation.

Candidate selection should reconstruct the affected transcript and translated sequence. A stop-gain terminates translation rather than adding a new amino acid; an unchanged upstream sequence alone does not specify a new mutant peptide. A frameshift can instead create an altered tail before stopping. Litchfield and colleagues found expressed frameshift changes enriched in positions predicted to escape decay and reported associations with checkpoint outcomes in melanoma cohorts, with additional immune-reactivity evidence from vaccine studies. These are context-specific findings, not a rule that every frameshift is expressed, displayed or useful. Mutant RNA and downstream presentation and recognition remain separate questions.

Consider a hypothetical message after splicing: its retained exons are joined in one continuous RNA, without an intron at each join. A translating ribosome has passed an earlier join but stops before a later one. An exon junction complex retained upstream of that later join is downstream of the stop and can support the junction-dependent surveillance route. Removing junction-associated proteins during translation is different from removing introns during splicing. In a second hypothetical message the stop lies in the final exon, with no downstream complex specified. That description alone does not measure RNA stability, exclude other decay mechanisms or demonstrate a normal protein. The positions are context for a hypothesis, not a universal distance threshold.

before.name: RNA splicing
before.tldr: RNA processing removes introns and joins retained exons. Different processing choices can produce different messages without changing the underlying gene sequence.
before.summary:
Splicing processes an initial RNA transcript. Exons are retained in a specified product and may contain untranslated sequence; introns are removed. For many nuclear pre-mRNAs, a spliceosome made of RNA and proteins recognizes boundary and regulatory sequences. The donor site starts an intron and the acceptor site ends it. Alternative choices yield transcript isoforms; a variant can alter exon inclusion, intron retention or use of a cryptic site. Exon skipping is not automatically a frameshift: the coding sequence and resulting joins matter. An altered message may undergo nonsense-mediated decay or produce a changed protein, but neither outcome follows from a prediction alone.

Cancer-associated splicing changes can arise through altered RNA-processing factors or their expression. SF3B1, SRSF2, U2AF1 and ZRSR2 illustrate studied factors; AR-V7 and BCL2L1 illustrate named transcript contexts. The linked review describes disease-specific mechanisms and therapeutic research. An altered transcript alone does not establish an intact abnormal protein, immune presentation, a therapeutic dependency or patient benefit. Free-drug development and a conjugated payload also require their own construct-specific evidence.

links.label: Bradley & Anczuków, RNA splicing dysregulation and the hallmarks of cancer (Nature Reviews Cancer 2023)
Intron function in the nonsense-mediated decay of beta-globin mRNA: indications that pre-mRNA splicing in the nucleus can influence mRNA translation in the cytoplasm.
A survey of best practices for RNA-seq data analysis (Genome biology 2016)

notes: Leading programmes: Abdel-Wahab (MSK) on spliceosome mutations; Bradley (Fred Hutch) on splicing and neoantigens; Ebert (Dana-Farber) on SF3B1 in MDS.

A junction read supports a local RNA join, not necessarily a complete isoform. Gene-level counts can hide transcript differences. RNA quality, read coverage, reference version and cell mixture affect interpretation; protein quantity and function need separate evidence.

The pathway drawing groups possible consequences studied in particular cancer systems. Its arrows do not mean that every splice change causes every listed outcome; protein formation, presentation and functional dependence require their own evidence.

Identify the reference sequence, including its version when the reference database uses versions. For an intronic change, HGVS uses a genomic reference together with the specified transcript used for coding coordinates; a mature transcript reference alone does not contain the intron. In an invented transcript whose exon ends at coding position 200, c.200+1G>A places a change one base into the following intron. The c. prefix gives coding-DNA coordinates and p. describes a protein consequence. The DNA name alone does not specify an exon skip, frameshift or remaining function; one DNA change can produce several RNA products.

In a fictional repair-gene example, a high gene-level RNA count can include abnormal splice products and messages from normal neighbours. A reproducible abnormal junction supports a local RNA join, rather than a complete transcript, its protein or its originating DNA allele. An intronic DNA base may be removed during processing, so a mature-junction read need not contain that base. Assigning the product to a particular allele needs suitable linking sequence or another justified allele-specific measurement, with cell-source and reference checks. RNA directly examines the processing product; the gene-level count cannot settle the protein-function question.
before.analogy: Splicing is like editing a recording into different versions. A changed edit can alter the final product, but the RNA join alone does not show which complete protein is made or what it does.
interventions: Spliceosome modulators (H3B-8800 negative; next generation in development)
PRMT5 inhibitors in MTAP-deleted and splicing-mutant cancers
Antisense oligonucleotides to redirect splicing (AR-V7, BCL2L1)

before.name: Ivonescimab
before.tldr: A Chinese bispecific that beat Keytruda head-to-head on progression-free survival in lung cancer, the first drug ever to do so.
before.summary: HARMONi-2 (China): PFS 11.1 vs 5.8 months versus pembrolizumab in PD-L1+ first-line NSCLC. Approved in China (2024) for EGFR-mutant NSCLC after TKI (HARMONi-A) and first-line PD-L1+ NSCLC. Summit Therapeutics holds Western rights; HARMONi (global, EGFR-mutant post-TKI) met PFS but OS was not statistically significant in 2025; HARMONi-3 (squamous and non-squamous first-line) ongoing. Spawned a wave of PD-(L)1×VEGF bispecifics (Pfizer/3SBio, BMS/BioNTech, Merck/LaNova).
before.mechanism: Tetravalent PD-1×VEGF-A bispecific with cooperative binding: VEGF binding increases PD-1 affinity, concentrating activity in tumour.

approvals.indication: EGFR-mutant NSCLC after TKI (with chemotherapy); first-line PD-L1+ NSCLC

mechanismSteps: Tetravalent antibody binds VEGF-A in the tumour microenvironment
VEGF binding increases the antibody's affinity for PD-1 (cooperative binding), concentrating it in tumour
PD-1 blockade releases T cells; VEGF neutralisation normalises vessels and reduces immunosuppressive myeloid cells

dosing.modifications: Standard immune-mediated event algorithm plus VEGF-class precautions (bleeding, hypertension, proteinuria)
dosing.monitoring: Blood pressure, urine protein, thyroid, LFTs
